trust_boundaries: async: order_service and payment_service to message_queue to inventory_service
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted e-commerce microservices platform with payment processing

threat_actors.name: External Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Payment data theft, order manipulation for financial gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: API endpoint exploitation via exposed gateway — OWASP API Top 10 vectors
non_capabilities: No direct database network access — all access via service APIs
No mTLS certificates for payment tier

threat_actors.name: Compromised Service Account
threat_actors.motivation: Lateral movement after gaining foothold in one microservice
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Service-to-service API token compromise via one vulnerable service
non_capabilities: No OS-level access outside compromised container
No admin credentials for message queue broker
No access to secrets manager directly

attack_paths.impact: API gateway bypass or exploitation to reach internal services directly
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: API gateways are high-value targets; exploit complexity is moderate if versioning lags

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised user credentials via phishing or prior breach
attack_paths.impact: User account takeover, PII exposure from user_db
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: No MFA assumption; credential stuffing is highly automated

attack_paths.entry_point: Deserialization or injection in order processing logic
attack_paths.impact: Code execution within order_service container, access to order_db and message_queue
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Deserialization vulnerabilities are common in Java/Node microservices; requires finding specific endpoint

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious message injected via message_queue after AP-003
attack_paths.impact: Persistent access to payment_service, exposure of payment card data in payment_db
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires chained exploit (AP-003 first); payment tier has additional mTLS controls

attack_paths.entry_point: Access via compromised payment_service from AP-004
attack_paths.impact: Mass exfiltration of payment card records
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-003 and AP-004 success; high detection probability during exfil volume

attack_paths.entry_point: Admin API endpoint after AP-002 account takeover
attack_paths.impact: Creation of backdoor admin account for persistent access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Admin API endpoints are commonly insufficiently protected in microservices without centralised RBAC

mitigations.control_name: API Gateway access controls and WAF
Message queue authentication and message signing
Data loss prevention and egress monitoring
Centralised RBAC with audit logging for admin operations

findings.severity_rationale: Payment card data is reachable via chained exploit through message queue; PCI-DSS scope makes this a regulatory-grade finding
No MFA means any credential stuffing campaign can compromise user accounts at scale
Deserialization in order service provides direct code execution path; common and exploitable in microservice frameworks
Admin account creation is possible after account takeover; lacks RBAC gate preventing self-elevation
API gateway WAF is partial; specific bypass techniques exist for common WAF deployments
